skills/handoff/scripts/feather_handoff/h.change: Local fix pending upstream: legacy-format entry starts are recognized only before the first modern entry, so archived bodies with legacy-looking lines stay archivable. History byte offsets are computed in one incremental pass. Local change (handoff-worktree-store 01): history and archive paths from the store object.

Local fix pending upstream: clear and seal parse archive sources under their queried archive/<batch>.md name. clear checks for pending completed work like seal and defers with pending-archive. A malformed or unreadable work file blocks clear and seal with pending-unknown when it may be completed: unreadable, no title on the first line, or not exactly one 狀態 line reading 進行中 or 受阻; other malformed works are re-checked before writing and reported in warnings. After the selected-identity check, a work without format problems also blocks clear and seal with pending-unknown when its whole text has more than one status line or a merge-conflict marker line (<<<<<<<, >>>>>>> or ||||||| at the line start followed by a space or the line end). Local change (handoff-worktree-store 01): history and archive paths from the store object. Local change (handoff-worktree-store 03): in a shared run clear propagates a denied replacement as the store-unwritable error, and seal propagates it when the call wrote no destination; a seal that already wrote its destination keeps the partial seal-failed result with destination_version and adds cause_code store-unwritable. A checkout-local store keeps the previous partial results.

skills/handoff/scripts/feather_handoff/a.change: Local fix pending upstream: completed work is checked for exact archivability (check_archivable) and reported as format with a reword/replacement hint; title line compared after stripping; CRLF histories get CRLF marker and separator, and a CRLF separator before a following entry is accepted on retry. archive accepts an optional tracking (default or track) and applies it after a successful archival, returning partial tracking-failed with archived true when tracking fails; the archival run by a completed save does not apply it again. An empty or whitespace-only history is framed like a new one. A tracking failure after archival with cause_code promisor-remote or promisor-unknown names the Git upgrade or removal of the promisor configuration in its recovery instead of resolving the Git rules. Local change (handoff-worktree-store 01): history path from the store object. Local change (handoff-worktree-store 02): archive refuses a track choice in a run that uses the shared store before writing. Local change (handoff-worktree-store 03): an explicit archive whose history write the shared store denies propagates it as the store-unwritable error; the archival run by a completed save keeps the partial history-save-failed result and recovery, adding cause_code store-unwritable in a shared run.

skills/handoff/scripts/feather_handoff/w.change: Local fix pending upstream: create/update refuse a 完成 save whose body would not archive; a completed work accepts one reviewed replacement keeping title, 更新 and 狀態：完成 when history lacks that identity; update details follow the file newline. A details update that would hide or change the level-1/2 sections after the managed details is refused with details-format; create/update results add warnings for level-1/2 headings inside details and update results add preserved_sections. An archival failure after a completed save returns partial archive-failed with cause_code and recovery retry-archive. The details-update sibling check compares headings together with their offsets inside the verbatim tail. A completed save whose tracking failed recommends archive with the same tracking choice. A details update is refused with details-format when the old details hide level-1/2 headings in a fence left open at the end or in a fence holding a same-character opener with an info string. Blank optional fields are input errors; create normalizes CRLF and CR in details to LF. Details-update section checks use the CommonMark ATX heading rule (baseline.level). A tracking failure with cause_code git-unavailable keeps the partial tracking-failed result but its recovery says to wait for Git, not to repeat create or update now, and once Git runs to apply tracking once with update (active work) or archive (completed work) using the same tracking choice. Partial header updates end the header at baseline.header_end. A tracking failure with cause_code promisor-remote or promisor-unknown keeps the partial tracking-failed result; its recovery says not to retry, to upgrade Git to 2.45.0 or later or have the user remove the promisor configuration, and then to apply tracking once with update (active work) or archive (completed work). Local change (handoff-worktree-store 01): history path from the store object. Local change (handoff-worktree-store 02): create and update refuse a track choice in a run that uses the shared store before writing. Local change (handoff-worktree-store 03): the archival run by a completed save passes denied_as_error=False, so a shared-store denial of the history write keeps the partial history-save-failed result.

skills/handoff/scripts/feather_handoff/c.change: Local fix pending upstream: invalid JSON, non-UTF-8 or too deeply nested stdin is an input error, and any unexpected exception becomes a JSON internal error with exit 2. Usage errors use the JSON envelope with code usage and a missing selected file is not-found (exit 2); --help stays plain text. A FileNotFoundError is not-found only for a file inside the selected project (or, without a file name, for read/archive/compare of a named work); otherwise io. A duplicate JSON key on stdin is an input error. --project and --exact-root are accepted before or after the subcommand. Local change (handoff-worktree-store 01): partial reads when either the Working checkout or the Handoff store is uncertain; not-found within either location. Local change (handoff-worktree-store 03): an error that Store.unwritable reports (a denied creation in the shared store) has code store-unwritable, store (the store directory) and access write, and its message names the store, the write access the session needs, and that nothing was written in the Working checkout in its place; a checkout-local store keeps its previous code.

skills/handoff/scripts/feather_handoff/s.change: Local fix pending upstream: superscript COM and LPT names are reserved. read_file change detection ignores st_ctime (stat and fstat disagree on Windows with Python 3.12+). A linked --project path or ancestor above the project is resolved once with a strict realpath and registered as the trusted root; check_path stops at that root after confirming it still resolves to itself. The Git root is the resolved path or its nearest ancestor that is the Git top level; a path crossing a link below the repository root is uncertain. Volumes without strict realpath keep the previous full-ancestor link checks. create_file removes the partial file it created when writing fails (same st_dev/st_ino) and re-raises the original error. git_environment also removes Git's remaining local repository variables (GIT_IMPLICIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_PREFIX, GIT_GRAFT_FILE, GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS, GIT_REPLACE_REF_BASE, GIT_SHALLOW_FILE, GIT_CONFIG) and GIT_REDIRECT_STDIN/STDOUT/STDERR while keeping user configuration variables; a successful root discovery with empty or non-absolute output is uncertain instead of the current directory. work_path and work_paths share one work-name rule (.md suffix after a nonempty stem, not history.md). replace_file makes its temporary file writable before removing it, suppresses cleanup errors and reports a failed replacement of a target without the write bit as read-only. Only symbolic links and name-surrogate reparse points count as links; a zero lstat tag with the reparse attribute is taken from the parent directory listing, and a missing entry or zero tag stays refused. run_git is the only place the tool starts Git: every command is git --no-pager --no-optional-locks -c core.fsmonitor= -C <directory> <arguments> with git_environment, a 5-second timeout and UTF-8 text, so no configured pager or fsmonitor runs and no optional index refresh is written; it needs no Store, and root discovery uses it. lazy_fetch_guard reads the effective configuration with includes followed (git config --list --includes -z) for a promisor remote (extensions.partialClone, or remote.<name>.promisor not set to false, or remote.<name>.partialclonefilter); only then is git version read. It returns whether every later command must carry --no-lazy-fetch (Git 2.45.0 or later), which run_git adds after its global options when called with no_lazy_fetch=True, and raises promisor-remote on an older Git and promisor-unknown when the configuration or version cannot be established. Git lookup (0.22.0): run_git never starts the bare name git. resolve_git walks PATH in order and considers only fully qualified entries (Windows: a drive letter followed by a separator, or a UNC path, after removing one pair of surrounding double quotes, decided without ntpath.isabs, and holding no : but the drive letter's, a UNC entry none, because Git for Windows' MSYS layer splits a value at such a : for the programs it starts, nor any character in U+F000-U+F0FF, which that layer maps back to : and the other characters Windows forbids in names; POSIX: a path starting with / without a .. component, because the kernel follows a link before the .. after it (/var/run/../proc/self/cwd is /proc/self/cwd when /var/run links to /run), and outside /proc and /dev/fd, judged from the text with repeated separators and . ignored, without following links, because such a path can name the calling process's current directory), skipping empty, relative, drive-relative, rooted-without-drive, \\?\ and \\.\ and unexpanded entries; it returns the first entry joined with git.exe that is a regular file after following links (Windows) or with an executable git (POSIX), uses no shutil.which, os.get_exec_path or os.defpath, keeps no result and starts no process, and raises the FileNotFoundError subprocess.run raised for a missing git when none is found. PATHEXT is not applied and git.cmd and git.bat are excluded because cmd.exe parses a batch file's arguments again with its own quoting and expansion, so Git would not receive the arguments given; such an installation is reported as Git unavailable. Git starts from the resolved executable's directory with a PATH of only the considered entries, keeping an inherited GIT_EXEC_PATH only when its value, taken as is without removing quotes, holds no path separator (os.pathsep, since Git puts the value before its children's PATH) and is an entry the resolver would consider, so on Windows one with a : other than the drive letter's or a character in U+F000-U+F0FF is dropped (git_environment itself unchanged), and an absolute -C, so the process's current directory takes part neither in finding Git nor in Git's own lookups. GIT_COMMAND now holds only the options after the executable. Local change (handoff-worktree-store 01): Store separates the Working checkout (project) from the checkout holding the Handoff store (store_checkout); each strictly resolved location is registered; uncertain reasons per location; root reports checkout, store and shared. Local change (handoff-worktree-store 02): _select_store gives an untracked linked worktree (absolute Git directory and common directory with different identities) the main worktree's store: the first NUL record of git worktree list --porcelain -z, accepted only when not bare, strictly resolved, outside the common directory, its own top level with a .git entry and the common directory as its Git directory, registered and path-checked; any failure, including tracking detection, makes the root uncertain with the Working checkout as the read scope. Local change (handoff-worktree-store 03): create_file (its parent directories and the exclusive open) and replace_file (its temporary file) tag an OSError as a denied creation when the operating system or the session sandbox denied it (Windows ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED or ERROR_WRITE_PROTECT; otherwise EACCES, EPERM or EROFS) and re-raise it unchanged; a sharing violation, a failed replacement of an existing target and every other error are not tagged. Store.unwritable is true for a tagged error only when root.shared is true. Local change (handoff-worktree-store 03 fix): create_file tags a failed exclusive open only when nothing exists at the target, since Windows reports EACCES without winerror for a directory already at that path.

skills/handoff/scripts/feather_handoff/o.change: Local fix pending upstream: source change detection ignores st_ctime (stat and fstat disagree on Windows with Python 3.12+). Duplicate-source detection uses the resolved path when st_ino is unavailable. git_observation runs Git through storage.run_git, decoding with errors=replace as before. Its rev-parse and symbolic-ref read no object; before show-ref --verify, which checks that the unresolved branch's object exists and can therefore fetch it, git_observation runs lazy_fetch_guard and passes its result to show-ref (--no-lazy-fetch on Git 2.45.0 or later); on promisor-remote or promisor-unknown it skips show-ref and returns an unknown Git observation with that code as its reason (OSError or a timeout there is git-unavailable). An observation whose HEAD resolves runs no detection. Local change (handoff-worktree-store 01): comment that observations use the Working checkout.

skills/handoff/scripts/feather_handoff/t.change: Local fix pending upstream: tracking: track removes only the exact /.feather/handoffs/ rule and records the '# cc-feather: track /.feather/handoffs/' comment marker in one write; a default save with that marker reports existing-rule and writes nothing. .gitignore lines are compared as Git reads them (rule_line): leading whitespace is part of the pattern and trailing spaces are not, so an indented marker does not count and track keeps an indented user rule. A first Git probe that cannot run Git or times out raises git-unavailable instead of returning not-checked, so the save reports partial tracking-failed. git runs Git through storage.run_git with strict UTF-8 decoding as before. Before the first command that can read objects (ls-files, check-ignore) and before any .gitignore write, ensure_tracking runs lazy_fetch_guard (OSError or a timeout there is git-unavailable) and passes its result to every later command; promisor-remote and promisor-unknown stop tracking before any object read or write. A default save under the track marker returns existing-rule before that check, as it reads no object and writes nothing. Local change (handoff-worktree-store 01): Git commands, the lazy-fetch guard and .gitignore run in the checkout that holds the store. Local change (handoff-worktree-store 02): detect_tracking reads the track marker and ls-files in the Working checkout after its own lazy-fetch guard while the store is chosen; require_track_choice refuses track with input in a run that uses the shared store.

skills/handoff/scripts/feather_handoff/b.change: Local fix pending upstream: headings follow the CommonMark ATX rule (up to three spaces of indent, one to six #, then a space, a tab or the line end) through level(), so indented and tab-separated headings bound the managed sections. header_end finds the end of a work header at the first such heading outside a code fence, splitting lines only at LF; a heading inside a fence does not end the header and an unclosed fence runs it to the end of the text.

skills/handoff/scripts/feather_handoff/r.change: Local fix pending upstream: read/list report a whitespace-only work title as a format problem (Work title must not be blank). The summary reads the header up to baseline.header_end, the fence-aware ATX boundary, instead of the first column-0 '#' heading followed by a space.
